title: AKT and ERK phosphorylate MDM2 at Ser186 and Ser188 promoting p53 degradation in breast cancer cells
abstract: Both AKT and ERK kinases directly phosphorylate the MDM2 protein at Ser186 and Ser188, which enhances MDM2-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of p53. Treatment with the AKT inhibitor MK-2206 or the MEK inhibitor PD98059 impaired this phosphorylation in MCF-7 and T47D breast cancer cells, leading to apoptosis.

title: EGFR autophosphorylation at Y1068 activates downstream STAT3 signaling in lung adenocarcinoma
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) autophosphorylation at tyrosine 1068 was shown to recruit GRB2 and activate STAT3 signaling in PC-9 lung adenocarcinoma cells. Gefitinib blocked EGFR Y1068 autophosphorylation and downstream STAT3 activation.

title: A novel phosphoproteomic workflow for kinase substrate identification using TiO2 enrichment
abstract: We describe a method for phosphopeptide enrichment using TiO2 chromatography coupled with LC-MS/MS for global phosphoproteome profiling. The workflow was validated using HeLa cell lysates and identified over 10,000 phosphosites.

title: p300 acetylates p53 at K382 enhancing its transcriptional activity in colon cancer
abstract: The acetyltransferase p300 directly acetylates p53 at lysine 382 in response to DNA damage. This acetylation enhances p53 DNA binding and transcriptional activation of p21. Treatment with the p300 inhibitor C646 impaired p53 K382 acetylation and reduced p21 expression in HCT116 colon cancer cells.

title: JAK2 phosphorylates STAT3 at Y705 promoting cell proliferation in myeloproliferative neoplasms
abstract: JAK2 kinase directly phosphorylates STAT3 at tyrosine 705, leading to STAT3 dimerization and nuclear translocation. Treatment with ruxolitinib, a JAK2 inhibitor, impaired STAT3 Y705 phosphorylation and reduced proliferation of HEL92.1.7 leukemia cells in a dose-dependent manner.
